text:
Darren Raddysh grew up in Toronto, went undrafted, and spent years in the AHL before Tampa Bay turned him into a 70-point defenseman last season. Now he's a Maple Leaf, logging 23:54 a night, and the timing has been rough: Toronto has won one of his last ten games.

He's still doing his part. Raddysh has 16 points in 25 games, 10 on the power play, and 62 shots. What he doesn't have is goals: 1 on 3.2 expected, a 1.6% shooting percentage against a likely range of 5.7% to 8.9%. With a top shot of 97.9 mph, 97th percentile in the league, that number won't stay there. Our middle projection still has him at 13 goals.

Evolving-Hockey rated him 15th among 215 defensemen last season, built mostly on even-strength offense, though with strong teammates in Tampa. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the home-plate area more than nearly any defenseman. Yahoo Sports asked whether he's surprised by how head coach Jim Hiller has used him. His answer, in the headline: "Trying To Do My Best." For a hometown kid on a losing team, that sounds about right.
headline: Raddysh comes home and keeps creating
